title: sec-sophon-sdk-ts: HTTPS not enforced — silent http:// basePath downgrade leaks Bearer key
description: From security audit (sophon-sdk-typescript-9k7). Configuration.basePath (src/runtime.ts:34-36) and the Sophon facade (src/helpers/sophon.ts:60-93) accept any basePath, including http://, with no warning or guard. SOPHON_BASE_URL in README defaults to https but nothing prevents a plaintext downgrade, which would send 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' in cleartext. Checklist (SDK block) requires: refuse plaintext http:// unless caller explicitly opts in (allowInsecure:true) with a loud warning. Fix: in the Sophon facade, throw on http:// basePath unless allowInsecure:true; warn loudly when opted in. Acceptance: http:// basePath rejected by default; allowInsecure:true permits it with console.warn.
acceptance_criteria: http:// basePath throws by default; allowInsecure:true allows it with a loud warning; https unaffected; test covers both.
close_reason: Sophon facade now rejects http:// basePath by default (throws), allows it only with allowInsecure:true + a loud console.warn. https/relative/default pass through. Verified 4 cases.

title: sec-sophon-sdk-ts: .gitignore missing .env* and .npmrc
description: From security audit (sophon-sdk-typescript-9k7). .gitignore lacks .env* and .npmrc. Universal checklist requires these be ignored to prevent accidental commit of a real SOPHON_API_KEY (verify/smoke scripts use process.env.SOPHON_API_KEY) or an npm auth token. Fix: add '.env', '.env.*', '!.env.example', and '.npmrc' to .gitignore. Acceptance: .gitignore ignores .env files and .npmrc.

title: sec-sophon-sdk-ts: download helper follows redirect Location to any host (open follower)
description: From security audit (sophon-sdk-typescript-9k7). src/helpers/downloads.ts:75-89 reads the 302 Location header and fetches new URL(location, base) with default redirect mode (follow). No host allowlist; second fetch is an open follower. Checklist (Sophon-platform protocols) requires: follow exactly one redirect, only to allowlisted hosts (*.backblazeb2.com / f00X.backblazeb2.com). Auth header is correctly NOT forwarded to the redirect target, so the API key does not leak; risk is SSRF/open-follow if the API returns an unexpected/compromised Location. Fix: validate location host against an allowlist, set redirect:'error' (or manual+single-hop) on the presigned fetch, reject non-https. Acceptance: malicious Location host rejected; only one hop followed; unit test for allowlist.
acceptance_criteria: Location host validated against B2 allowlist; only one redirect hop; non-allowlisted/non-https Location rejected with a clear error; unit test covers reject + accept.
close_reason: downloads.ts now validates the 302 Location against an HTTPS + host allowlist (*.backblazeb2.com + API origin + caller-supplied), follows exactly one hop (redirect:'error'), throws UnsafeRedirectError otherwise. Auth header still not forwarded to presigned host. Verified: B2/api-origin pass, evil host + non-https rejected.

title: sec-sophon-sdk-ts: harden npm publish (OIDC Trusted Publishing / GH Environment) + confirm 2FA on publisher
description: From security audit (sophon-sdk-typescript-9k7). publish.yml already uses --provenance with id-token:write (good), but auth uses a long-lived repo-level secret NPM_TOKEN. Universal/CI checklist prefers short-TTL/env-scoped publishing tokens. Also, '2FA on publisher account' (SDK block) cannot be verified from the repo and must be confirmed manually. Fix: migrate to npm OIDC Trusted Publishing (tokenless) or move NPM_TOKEN into a protected GitHub Environment with a granular short-lived token; confirm 2FA-required is enabled on the @liqhtworks npm publisher. Acceptance: tokenless OIDC publish OR env-scoped token; publisher 2FA confirmed.
acceptance_criteria: Publish uses npm OIDC Trusted Publishing or an env-scoped short-lived token; 2FA-on-publish confirmed on the npm account.
notes:
Deferred to infra/manual: provenance already on. Did NOT rip out NODE_AUTH_TOKEN unilaterally (npm OIDC Trusted Publishing needs a trusted publisher configured on npmjs.com first, else publish breaks). Owner action: (1) configure npm Trusted Publishing for @liqhtworks/sophon-sdk + switch publish.yml to tokenless OIDC, OR move NPM_TOKEN to a protected GitHub Environment with a granular token; (2) confirm 2FA-required on the npm publisher account.
Reassigned to Gabe (Liqhtworks) — needs npm-side Trusted Publishing setup + 2FA confirmation on the @liqhtworks npm publisher account; both are account/infra actions outside this repo.

title: sec-sophon-sdk-ts: README — document API key least-privilege scoping + rotation; link AUP

title: sec-sophon-sdk-ts: commit package-lock.json so CI runs npm ci (reproducible installs)
description: From security audit (sophon-sdk-typescript-9k7). package-lock.json is untracked (git status), so publish.yml's 'if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then npm ci; else npm install' falls back to npm install — non-reproducible. Low impact today (zero runtime deps) but the lockfile should be committed and CI should use --frozen/npm ci. Fix: commit package-lock.json. Acceptance: lockfile committed; CI uses npm ci.
acceptance_criteria: package-lock.json committed; CI install step uses npm ci.
notes: package-lock.json (zero runtime deps) will be committed with the fix/security-audit-findings branch; publish.yml already runs 'npm ci' when the lockfile is present, so no CI change needed.

title: sec-sophon-sdk-ts: verifyWebhookSignature should accept multiple secrets for rotation overlap
description: From security audit (sophon-sdk-typescript-9k7). src/helpers/webhooks.ts accepts a single 'secret'. The platform protocol documents overlapping signing-key rotation windows where clients must accept either key. The helper can't verify against multiple secrets during rotation. Enhancement: allow secret: string | string[] (or secrets: string[]) and pass if any matches via constant-time compare. Acceptance: verify accepts an array of secrets; passes if any matches; still constant-time per candidate.
acceptance_criteria: verifyWebhookSignature accepts multiple candidate secrets and verifies against each with constant-time compare.
close_reason: verifyWebhookSignature secret now accepts string | string[]; verifies against each candidate with constant-time compare, passes if any matches. Backward compatible. Verified multi-secret + single + reject.
